ev.q: This report summarizes these ACIP recommendations and the rationale, including evidence reviewed by the ACIP COVID-19 Vaccines Work Group (Work Group) and presented to ACIP.
VE of a 2023–2024 COVID-19 vaccine dose among persons with immunocompromise was 36% (95% CI = 22%–48%) 7–59 days after vaccination
In persons without immunocompromise, VE was 51% (95% CI = 45%–56%) 7–59 days after vaccination
The societal incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) for an additional dose of COVID-19 vaccine in persons aged ≥65 years was $356,534

public_health_question.v: Should adults aged ≥65 years and persons aged ≥6 months with moderate or severe immunocompromise receive additional doses of 2024–2025 COVID-19 vaccine?

equity.level_reason: Age bounds and immunocompromise define the target populations; no SPD-specific results. Equity appears only as a generic implementation consideration (equitable access).

level_alternative.reason: Equitable access to vaccination is raised as an implementation consideration, which could count as equity raised only as a recommendation.

ev.q: Adults aged ≥65 years should receive 2 doses of 2024–2025 COVID-19 vaccine

notes: All VE, safety and cost-effectiveness figures are cited from earlier reports and presented to ACIP; the article computes nothing of its own, so method fields are empty. Design follows the named ACIP GRADE/EtR process. Vaccine outcome type reflects the cited VE evidence underlying the recommendation.
